4.text: descent, the “old male companions,” are also called “those of the same fire”

5.text: (ᴇnnaˊn-yɪˊnlaᵋt), because they have community of fire. Paternal relationship

6.text: is considered to be much stronger than maternal relationship. There is a

7.text: Chukchee saying which has it that even a distant relative on the father’s side

48.text: and “mother” respectively, in reality have the meaning “old man” and “old woman.” Both are derived from

49.text: ɪnp, the root of the adjective nɪˊnpɪqên (“he is old”).

50.text: ⁵ In all derivations, only the first stem is used. Tuˊmg̣ɪtum (pl. tuˊmg̣ɪt, stem tuˊmg̣ɪ) means “companion,”

51.text: “mate,” also “kinsman.” A husband, speaking of his wife, calls her g̣ŭmniˊn tuˊmg̣ɪtum (my mate”). G̣etuˊmg̣ɪlin

52.text: means “one with companions,” “one with kinsmen,” “one with influence.” It is used as a compound in several

53.text: terms referring to degrees of relationship, in various combinations, sometimes only between males, at other times

54.text: only between females, and even also between males and females.

55.text: ⁶ The terms for “elder brother” and “younger brother” are relative; i. e., all brothers older than myself

56.text: are my ɪneˊelit, and all brothers younger than myself are my ᴇʟeˊnyut (pl.). More detailed terms are used as

57.text: follows: ênaˊn-ɪnaˊalɪn, “the oldest brother;” ênaˊn-ᴇʟaˊñê, “the youngest brother;” wuˊthɪtčeᵋn, “the middle

58.text: (brother).” ɪneˊelin (“elder brother”) and ᴇʟeˊñi (“younger brother”) are used both by males and females; but

59.text: the former term is pronounced by women ɪniˊnelin, according to the rules of female pronunciation, in which

60.text: contractions are avoided. The elder sister is also called ɪneˊelin or ɪniˊnelin (by males and females). ᴇʟeˊñi is

61.text: used for the younger brother only.
